ai.title: Assistant terminal commands locked to project root
ai.summary: Assistant mode in runCommandPty now forces cwd to project root via cd ${projectRoot} and bypasses directory tracking. run_terminal_command description updated to 'Execute a CLI command from the project root' and removed persistent cwd note. Affects backend/src/tools.ts and npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts. Assistant commands resolve with 'Ran command from project root' status; user mode retains cd tracking.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to run a terminal command, it will now always run that command starting from your project's main folder, no matter what directory you thought it was in. You'll see the project root path printed at the start of the command output, and afterward the assistant will report that the command was run from the project root. This change only applies to commands the assistant runs automatically; if you type your own terminal commands, the old behavior of remembering your current directory still works.

ai.title: Add cwd parameter to runterminalcommand
ai.summary: Added optional cwd parameter to run_terminal_command tool schema and handler. This allows the agent to execute commands from specific directories rather than being restricted to the project root. Implementation updates backend tool definitions, common constants, and npm-app terminal utilities to support directory resolution and proper path display.

eli5.text: You can now tell the assistant to run a terminal command from a specific folder instead of always forcing it back to the project's main folder. Previously, even if you mentioned a file by its path, the assistant had to guess whether it lived in your current directory or the project root and then run the command from the project root anyway; now it can run straight from wherever that folder actually is. If you watched the terminal, you would see the folder name in the command prompt stay correct instead of jumping back to the topmost project folder.

ai.title: Reduce max consecutive assistant messages
ai.summary: Lowered `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES` from 20 to 12 in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This tightens the limit on consecutive assistant messages within a single turn. The change applies to the backend core logic.

eli5.text: The assistant is no longer allowed to send as many replies in a row. Previously, it could produce up to twenty consecutive messages within a single interaction, but that limit has been lowered to twelve. If you were watching the assistant run, you might notice that it stops or hands control back to you sooner than it used to. This change is already live and affects how the backend core logic behaves today.

ai.title: Saxy parser emits rawTag text for stray XML
ai.summary: Saxy parser now attaches `rawTag` to `TagOpenNode` and `TagCloseNode`. `xml-stream-parser` forwards this raw text to `onText` when encountering stray or unknown XML tags. This prevents silent loss of malformed agent output by treating invalid tags as plain text. Covers `backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts` and `common/src/util/saxy.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes XML-like tags that don't match the expected format, the system now keeps the text of those stray tags and shows them as plain text instead of silently dropping them. This means you'll see the raw, malformed tags in the output rather than having them disappear, so you can tell what the assistant actually generated even when it produces invalid tags.

ai.title: Fix terminal cd command in runCommandPty
ai.summary: Merged `cd` command into `runCommandPty` execution string to ensure working directory applies before user command. Removed separate `ptyProcess.write` for initial `cd` and unified Windows/Unix command construction with `cd` prefix. Prevents race conditions where `cd` might not execute before subsequent commands. Affects `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the terminal to run a command in a specific folder, the program now tells the terminal to switch to that folder first and then run your command, all as a single coordinated step. Previously, the folder switch and the command were sent separately, which sometimes caused the command to start before the folder change finished. You wouldn't notice this change directly, but it makes sure commands always start in the correct folder and run more reliably, especially when switching between Windows and other systems.

ai.title: Add carriage returns to newline squashing logic
ai.summary:
Updated `npm-app/src/display.ts` to normalize newlines by inserting carriage returns (`
`) before applying squash logic. The `previous` buffer now tracks 4 chars instead of 2 to handle the multi-character sequence, and regex patterns in `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write` were adjusted to match `
{3,}` instead of `
{3,}`. This ensures consistent line ending handling across the CLI output stream.

eli5.text: When you run a command in your terminal, the assistant's output sometimes had runs of blank lines that looked messy. Now, every line break in the assistant's terminal output includes both a carriage return and a newline (the standard Windows-style line ending), which lets the tool correctly detect and collapse any run of three or more blank lines down to just two. You won't notice a visual difference unless the assistant was already printing lots of blank lines, in which case they'll appear slightly more consistent. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that's already in place today.

ai.title: Add chargeUser flag to prevent billing filepicker training data
ai.summary: Backend adds optional `chargeUser` boolean to `promptClaude`, `promptClaudeStream`, and `saveMessage` in `claude.ts` and `message-cost-tracker.ts`. `getRelevantFilesForTraining` in `request-files-prompt.ts` passes `chargeUser: false` to skip billing for internal filepicker training requests. `saveMessage` zeroes out `costInCents` when `chargeUser` is false, defaulting to true otherwise. Scope limited to backend Claude API and cost tracking modules.

eli5.text: When you open the file picker to help train the assistant on your own files, you will no longer be charged for that usage; behind the scenes, the system now marks those particular training requests as free before calculating any bill. The pricing logic was updated to honor that flag, defaulting to charging you as before for all your other messages and conversations. This is a backend-only adjustment, so you won't see any settings change; if anything, you just avoid a small charge next time you let the assistant learn from a file you select.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer saves detailed file-reading information to its internal training logs when you haven't explicitly asked it to look at any files. For you, this simply means less unnecessary data is being collected behind the scenes during casual chats where no specific files are involved. The system now checks first whether any files were actually requested before deciding to record expanded file context for training purposes. This change went live on May 13, 2025.

eli5.text: The assistant now looks at two different sets of files at once - the most important ones for your request and the ones that aren't obvious but might still be useful - and combines them into a single list. Behind the scenes, it filters out duplicates, checks that the files actually exist, and cuts the list down to a maximum number so you get the best suggestions without overload. If you asked for help with a project, you'd see slightly more relevant files suggested now than before, since the system is pulling from a broader but smarter set. This is live today.

ai.title: File processing returns error strings instead of null
ai.summary: processFileBlock and processStrReplace now return discriminated union types containing an error string instead of null on failure. mainPrompt.ts updates the fileProcessingPromisesByPath type to accommodate these error objects and passes the error message through to the user. This replaces silent skips with actionable feedback for common issues like missing old strings or unchanged files.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to edit or create a file and something goes wrong, like the file doesn't exist, the old text you asked to replace can't be found, or nothing actually changed, it now tells you a clear reason instead of silently skipping the step. You'll see a short message explaining what happened, such as 'The file does not exist' or 'The old string was not found in the file,' so you can fix the problem and try again. This makes mistakes easy to spot and correct rather than leaving you wondering why a file didn't update.

ai.title: Remove endturn and awaittoolresults tools
ai.summary: Removed end_turn and await_tool_results tools from the agent loop. The system now automatically reprompts if tool results are pending, eliminating explicit turn-ending signals. Updated main-prompt.ts, tools.ts, websocket-action.ts, and common constants to reflect this change. Agent instructions and thinking stream prompts adjusted to remove references to these tools.

eli5.text: When you interact with the AI assistant, you no longer need to manually signal the end of a turn or wait for results, those steps happen automatically. Previously, the assistant had to explicitly call special tools to end a turn or pause for tool results, but now the system simply continues when results are ready. You would notice this if you looked and saw the assistant no longer mentions or triggers those extra steps, since everything is handled behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix undefined dereference in Saxy defaultEncoding
ai.summary: Added a fallback guard for `state.defaultEncoding` in `common/src/util/saxy.ts` to prevent undefined dereferences during `StringDecoder` initialization. The code now checks if `state` or `state.defaultEncoding` is undefined and defaults to 'utf8' if so. This change ensures stable stream processing in the Saxy XML parser.

eli5.text: When the assistant reads XML content to you, it sometimes tried to set up a text decoder with an encoding value that had not arrived yet, causing a crash. The code now waits and, if the expected encoding is missing, falls back to the standard 'utf8' text setting instead. You would notice fewer unexpected interruptions or errors while the assistant processes XML data.

ai.title: CLI prompt history deduplication logic updated
ai.summary: Prompt history deduplication now moves non-unique prompts to end instead of filtering them out during load. `addHistory` removes all previous occurrences of a trimmed line before appending it. This ensures readline history reflects the most recent usage order without losing context. Affects `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the up and down arrows to scroll through your recent prompts, repeated prompts now jump to the end of the list instead of being hidden. Previously, typing the same prompt again would remove older copies from history; now they stay but move to the newest spot, keeping your context intact while still avoiding duplicate clutter. This only affects people who use the command-line version of the tool, and you'll notice it the next time you cycle through previously typed prompts.
